acid, 2300 USP units of vitamin A, 400 USP units of vitamin D, 1.2 mg of thiamin, 1.4

Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a chronic lung dis-
ease that commonly develops in the premature infant as a result 
of RDS and the mechanical ventilation and oxygen used to treat 
it. Because of the role of vitamin A in facilitating tissue repair, 
and because of reports of preterm infants having low vitamin A 
stores, large supplemental doses of vitamin A have been sug-
gested for the prevention of BPD. One report suggests that 
providing ELBW premature infants with IM injections of vita-
min A at 5000 units/day three times per week during the first 
month of life decreases the incidence of BPD (Tyson et al,
